In this study, utilizing deep imaging from the HATSP and HATPS surveys, we quantified star formation (SF) suppression in early-type galaxies lacking a visible stellar population—defined as "dark" or "hidden" star formation—across a wide range of L* systems. Our findings reveal that approximately 20% of these galaxies exhibit clear evidence of recent or ongoing star formation being halted, a statistic that aligns closely with the proportion of spirals where star formation ceases upon the development of a bulge. This parallel strongly implies that bulge-induced quenching operates as a universal mechanism, applicable both within spiral galaxies and to the ensemble of dark bulges observed in early-type galaxies.

The method leverages the signature function, a technique previously employed for testing equivalence, to solve containment by assessing whether the signature function can distinguish the language of the subexpression from all other languages. Signature functions operate within a specific vector space, where each is represented as a vector; thus, containment is resolved by expressing the signature function of the subexpression as a linear combination of signature functions representing the candidates. The signature function of a regular expression is constructed as the composition of signature functions corresponding to its constituent subexpressions. The resulting algorithm runs in quadratic time relative to the size of the regex, a significant improvement over the prior best complexity of $O(n^{10})$.

This paper details the MuLEO arrangement, presents simulation results demonstrating its performance, and outlines plans for a laboratory test.
